newsitem.title: JAPAN: Currencies should reflect fundamentals -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: Currencies should reflect fundamentals -- BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a news conference on Wednesday that currencies should reflect economic fundamentals and that excessive moves in currencies are undesirable, which is the basis of the Group of Seven (G7) agreement in Berlin in February.
Matsushita also said that Japan's monetary policy should be based on overall economic conditions, including the effects of the currency markets on the economy.
Monetary policy should not be considered on the basis of dealing solely with currency movements or as a way to cope with current account balances, he said.
"Our goal is to manage our policy with the objective of continued growth without inflation...by considering the overall domestic economy, including the impact of the currency market on it," he said.
Asked about the recent move in Japan's overnight call rates slightly above the official discount rate, Matsushita said, "Our policy on how we adjust overnight call rates has not changed."
The BOJ has said that it will guide money market rates so that they are, on average, slightly lower than the official discount rate.
He also said that, if the BOJ were to change its stance, it would discuss it with policy-making board members and then inform the markets.
Matsushita said financial institutions were actively dealing with problem loans and restructuring their business.
Should any firm face liquidity problems in the process of its restructuring, the BOJ would do all it could to support it, in order to ensure stability in the financial system, he said.
Matsushita added that he did not think revisions to Japan's foreign exchange laws would have a major impact on Japanese monetary policy.
